text.zh: 杀人者既逃，存亡不可知，此辈皆诖误无罪，而反桎梏耶？
text.en: The killer has escaped and we do not even know whether he is alive or dead. These people are all innocent victims of mistaken implication—why should they be shackled?

text.zh: 国制，罪人七十免刑，为其血气已衰，不任刑也。媪既能杀二人，何谓衰老？
text.en: Under the law of the realm, criminals aged seventy are spared punishment because their vital force has waned and they can no longer endure it. Yet this woman was strong enough to kill two people—how can she be called decrepit?

text.zh: 小兒误杀同牧者，实无杀人意，难以定罪。
text.en: The boy killed his companion by accident and had no intent to kill; he cannot properly be convicted of murder.

text.zh: 必唱名给散，无虚增之数。
text.en: Distributions must be made only by calling out each recipient's name, with no inflated numbers on the rolls.

text.zh: 国制，设印以署公牍、防奸伪，何为封私书？况汝出国时，我尚在京，未为辽阳省官，今何故有书遗我？汝君臣何欺诈如是耶？
text.en: Under the law of the realm, seals exist to authenticate official documents and prevent fraud—why use one to seal a private letter? Moreover, when you left your country I was still in the capital and was not yet an official in Liaoyang—why should you now have a letter for me? Why are your sovereign and ministers so deceitful?

translationRepairs: His great-grandfather Sagisi had been tutor to the Prince of Liao, and Emperor Shizu had praised his virtue.
His grandfather Sagisi had been tutor to the Prince of Liao, and Emperor Shizu had praised his virtue.
大父 means paternal grandfather; rendering it as great-grandfather overstates the generation distance relative to 曾祖.
His great-grandfather Sagisi served as tutor to the Prince of Liao; the Shizu Emperor praised his worth.
His grandfather Sagisi served as tutor to the Prince of Liao; the Shizu Emperor praised his worth.
The literal field must likewise render 大父 as grandfather, not great-grandfather.
In 1346 he was promoted to right chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then transferred to Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.
In 1346 he was promoted to right chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then transferred to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
翰林學士承旨 is Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts; Expositor-in-Chief would be 侍講/侍讀, not 承旨.
In the sixth year of Zhizheng he was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then changed to Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.
In the sixth year of Zhizheng he was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then changed to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
Literal English mislabels 承旨 as Expositor-in-Chief; Recipient of Edicts is the correct title.
In 1347 he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat at the age of sixty-nine.
In 1347 he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate at the age of sixty-nine.
陝西行臺 is the Shaanxi Branch Censorate; 行臺 is not 行省 (Branch Secretariat).
In the seventh year of Zhizheng he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat; he was then sixty-nine years old.
In the seventh year of Zhizheng he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate; he was then sixty-nine years old.
Literal English wrongly maps 行臺 to Branch Secretariat; Branch Censorate matches the Chinese office.
His great-grandfather Guiyu served the Taizu Emperor and was officer in charge of the qielian kou qieshi.
His great-grandfather Guiyu served Emperor Taizu as the Keshig officer overseeing the qielian households.
管领怯怜口怯薛官 denotes a Keshig officer supervising qielian households; this renders the title while removing the unresolved transcription and awkward 'served the Taizu Emperor.'

Temuder then had Yuelutiemuer appointed vice commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting him from vice director of the palace to gentleman for managing affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.

Temuder then had Yuelutiemuer appointed vice commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting his civil prestige rank from Yazhong Dafu to Gentleman for Managing Affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.
亚中大夫 is a junior-third-rank civil prestige title, not a palace office. The established translation elsewhere in Yuan History is Yazhong Dafu.

Temuder then memorialized appointing Yuelutiemuer Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting him from Vice Director of the Palace to Gentleman for Managing Affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.

Temuder then memorialized appointing Yuelutiemuer Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting his civil prestige rank from Yazhong Dafu to Gentleman for Managing Affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.
Literal English likewise mistakes 亚中大夫 for a palace office; Yazhong Dafu is the established Yuan History rendering of this civil prestige title.
In the second year of Zhizheng he came to audience; the emperor wished to retain him; he declined because his mother's funeral had not yet been buried.
In the second year of Zhizheng he came to audience; the emperor wished to retain him; he declined because his mother had not yet been buried.
母丧未葬 means his deceased mother had not yet been buried; making the funeral the thing buried is ungrammatical and misreads 葬.
When Buyantemuer arrived, they advanced together.
When Buyantiemuer arrived, they advanced together.
The biography subject is Buyantiemuer (卜颜帖木兒); Buyantemuer drops the established medial syllable.
Before long Jiang Prefecture fell again and Xingji was killed.
Before long Jiang Prefecture fell again, and Xingji died fighting there.
In the context of the city's fall, 死之 means Xingji died fighting there; this preserves his connection to the defense without asserting a more specific manner of death.

Buyantemuer convened the generals and said: "The bandits are linked inside and out; if we wait until they finish building fortifications and live off the grain of the various counties, defeating them will truly be difficult.

Buyantiemuer convened the generals and said: "The bandits are linked inside and out; if we wait until they finish building fortifications and live off the grain of the various counties, defeating them will truly be difficult.
Literal English again misspells Buyantiemuer as Buyantemuer against 卜颜帖木兒.
Xingji from youth served in Emperor Renzong's hidden residence and was known for keen intelligence.
Xingji from youth served in Emperor Renzong's residence before accession and was known for keen intelligence.
潜邸 is the conventional term for a prince's household before accession, not a literally hidden residence.

Xingji ordered a secret arrest; eighteen wives, concubines, female musicians, and women were found; the case was complete; he was convicted and his property registered; from this the powerful held back their hands and the poor rejoiced.

Xingji ordered his secret arrest. Eighteen women, including wives, concubines, and female musicians, were found; once the case was complete, the monk was convicted and his property confiscated. From then on the powerful held back and the poor rejoiced.
In this judicial context 籍之 means confiscating the offender's property. The revision also resolves the compressed list and ambiguous pronouns in the literal draft.
Xingji's nephew Bohua and several dozen personal guards died fighting.
Xingji's nephew Bobuhua and several dozen personal guards died fighting.
伯不华 is Bobuhua; Bohua omits the middle syllable 不.
Xingji's nephew Bohua and several dozen personal guards died with them.
Xingji's nephew Bobuhua and several dozen personal guards died with them.
Literal English likewise truncates 伯不华 to Bohua; Bobuhua restores all three syllables.

He entered court as vice minister of works, associate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, and supervising censor; he was transferred to vice minister of revenue, promoted to minister, sent out as commissioner of the Yannan surveillance commission, and promoted five times to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

He entered court as vice minister of works, associate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, and supervising censor; he was transferred to vice minister of revenue, promoted to minister, sent out as commissioner of the Yannan surveillance commission, and after five further transfers became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
又五迁为 means after five further transfers he reached the office, not that he was promoted five times into that same office.

He entered as Vice Minister of Works, Associate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, appointed Supervising Censor, transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, promoted to Minister, sent out as Commissioner of the Yannan Surveillance Commission, and five times promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

He entered as Vice Minister of Works, Associate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, appointed Supervising Censor, transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, promoted to Minister, sent out as Commissioner of the Yannan Surveillance Commission, and after five further transfers became Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
Literal 'five times promoted to' misreads 又五迁为; the destination office comes after five transfers.
They therefore resolved to dispatch five hundred troops under guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qie to suppress the rebels and report afterward.
They therefore resolved to dispatch five hundred troops under guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qielai to suppress the rebels and report afterward.
怯来 is Qielai; truncating to Qie drops the second syllable 来.
They therefore resolved to dispatch five hundred troops, sending guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qie to suppress them and then report.
They therefore resolved to dispatch five hundred troops, sending guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qielai to suppress them and then report.
Literal English likewise truncates 怯来 to Qie; Qielai is the full name.
By autumn the court appointed Yirenzhenban left chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Huonichi left chancellor, both leading troops to Jiangxi.
By autumn the court appointed Yirenzhenban left chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Huonichi left vice chancellor, both leading troops to Jiangxi.
Chinese distinguishes 左丞相 (Yirenzhenban) from 左丞 (Huonichi); calling both left chancellor conflates two ranks.
By autumn the court appointed Yirenzhenban Left Chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Huonichi Left Chancellor, both leading troops to Jiangxi.
By autumn the court appointed Yirenzhenban Left Chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Huonichi Left Vice Chancellor, both leading troops to Jiangxi.
Literal English must keep Huonichi as Left Vice Chancellor (左丞), not Left Chancellor (左丞相).
In the ninth year, from Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service he was appointed Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy and Director of the Classics Mat lectures.
In the ninth year, after serving as Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service, he was appointed Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts and Director of the Classics Mat lectures.
翰林学士承旨 is Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, as already established at s0054; Expositor-in-Chief denotes a different Hanlin office.
In 1349, after serving as commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service, he was appointed Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy and director of the Classics Mat lectures.
In 1349, after serving as commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service, he was appointed Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts and director of the Classics Mat lectures.
The idiomatic field repeats the same mistranslation of 翰林学士承旨 and should use the established title Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.

Xingji ordered his secret arrest; eighteen wives, concubines, female musicians, and women were found; he was convicted and his property confiscated; from then on the powerful held back and the poor rejoiced.

Xingji had him secretly arrested. The search uncovered eighteen women, including wives, concubines, and female musicians. Once the case was complete, the monk was convicted and his property confiscated; thereafter the powerful restrained themselves, and the poor rejoiced.
The revision preserves the meaning of 星吉命掩捕之 and 罪而籍之 while making the monk the unambiguous object of arrest, conviction, and confiscation.

There is Left Chancellor Zhang Boyan, retired and living in Fuzhou; that man is well versed in military affairs—it is fitting to invite him with convenient ceremony, have him act in the affairs of left chancellor of this province, and specially charge him with dispatching the army—then perhaps matters can succeed."

There is a retired Left Vice Chancellor named Zhang Boyan living in Fuzhou. He is well versed in military affairs; we should invite him with appropriate ceremony, appoint him acting Left Vice Chancellor of this province, and give him sole charge of deploying the army. Then perhaps the situation can be saved."
Both instances of 左丞 denote Left Vice Chancellor, distinct from 左丞相; the revised literal field also restores a coherent recommendation in English.

There is the retired left chancellor Zhang Boyan living in Fuzhou; he is well versed in military affairs. We should invite him with appropriate ceremony, have him act as left chancellor of this province, and charge him with commanding the army—then perhaps we can succeed."

There is a retired left vice chancellor named Zhang Boyan living in Fuzhou. He knows military affairs well. We should invite him with appropriate ceremony, appoint him acting left vice chancellor of this province, and give him sole charge of deploying the army; then perhaps the situation can be saved."
The idiomatic field must likewise distinguish Left Vice Chancellor (左丞) from the higher Left Chancellor (左丞相).
